data.narrative:
Living Carbon, a Series A biotech company founded by Maddie Hall and Patrick Mellor, has raised $36M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of 3 public-sector peers (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private companies in Biotech & Health, though formal peer-median triangulation was not feasible due to insufficient narrow-stage comparable data.

Stage-progression methodology, the sole applicable quantitative approach, applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement to the $36M raised proxy, yielding $72M. This method assumes the next funding round will command a 2x premium to current capital deployed. No revenue data was available to anchor a public-comp P/S multiple (sector median: 5.6x), a standard biotech valuation lever that remains inaccessible for private companies. Peer-median comparison similarly failed to satisfy data sufficiency thresholds, with the broader 8-company peer set fragmented across stage and scale.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $61M–$83M (median: $72M), reflecting ±15% variance around the stage-progression point estimate. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue disclosure, limited fungible precedent among early-stage biotech peers at comparable scale, and volatility in public-sector biotech multiples. Given single-method reliance, this range should be treated as indicative rather than definitive, pending disclosure of operating metrics or execution milestones.
